crime_highlights: Rampersaud was attacked from behind, causing him to fall forward, at which point he was punched and kicked from the front.
Rampersaud was struck over the head with a beer bottle, and stabbed in the back seven times.
Rampersaud's lung was punctured, and his kidney was lacerated causing potentially fatal internal bleeding.
the Appellant Vang moved to hit Reidt over the head with a beer bottle
rationale_highlights: The mitigating circumstances include the fact that the attack was not planned and cannot be said to be entirely unprovoked, in that there were apparently racial slurs made at the time.
note: Racial slurs came from the victim; not a systemic factor about the offenders.

crime_highlights: Both victims were subjected to gratuitous and serious acts of violence.
the appellant hit him in the face
The victim suffered a lacerated upper lip and broken jaw; his face was badly bruised and he lost four teeth.
the appellant attacked a second victim, a taxi driver, with a broken bottle.
This victim suffered four stitches to his nose, three stitches to his lip, and minor lacerations to his forehead.
rationale_highlights: Gladue mandates a different approach to sentencing aboriginals because of the systemic or background factors that play a part in bringing them before the court.
the hardships he has suffered should be taken into account in determining a fit sentence
We think that in the light of s. 718.2(e) of the Code and in the light of the nexus between the two offences
note: Para 12 on nexus with systemic disadvantage omitted for length.

crime_highlights: The complainant is the half sister of the respondent and at the time of the offence was 14 years old.
the complainant was placed in the respondent's home as a foster child
there were a series of sexual contacts between the respondent and the complainant
rationale_highlights: My primary reason for coming to that conclusion concerns the application of s. 718.2(e) of the Criminal Code
Gladue and Wells require a different approach to the sentencing of aboriginal offenders because of systemic or background circumstances.
The same can be said of this respondent.
such a disposition is consistent with s. 718.2(e) of the Code
